messages:
micah: New hire hit a subtle packaging trap in onboarding. They followed the "poetry -> export -> pip install -r requirements.txt" flow we document and ended up missing optional deps (aiohttp) used by the async client. App crashed with ModuleNotFoundError.

micah: Minimal repro:
```
# what they did
poetry install --no-root
poetry export --format requirements.txt --output requirements.txt
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -c \"from redwood.client import async_client\"  # -> ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'aiohttp'
```

micah: The exported requirements.txt contains `redwood-python-sdk==0.12.0` but no `redwood-python-sdk[async]` or the transitive deps for that extra.

micah: requirements.txt excerpt:
```
redwood-python-sdk==0.12.0
other-dep==1.2.3
```

yara: Ah — poetry export doesn't include extras unless you pass `--extras` (or select them in pyproject). If the quickstart assumes `poetry export` will include extras it is wrong. Our docs say "export a requirements.txt for CI" but don't show how to include extras.

tom: Two ways to fix: update docs to show `poetry export --without-hashes --extras "async" --format requirements.txt -o requirements.txt`, or change quickstart to rely on `poetry install` in the venv rather than piping exported requirements. For CI that needs pip-only, we must document the `--extras` usage.

zoe: Also a gotcha: if you export with extras, poetry will inline extras as separate requirement lines only for the package that declares them, e.g. `redwood-python-sdk[async]==0.12.0`. Some CI pipelines disallow bracket extras in pinned files; in that case you need to run `poetry export --extras "async" --format requirements.txt --output requirements.txt --without-hashes --add-extras` (or manually append the extra requirements). We should add examples for both cases.

micah: Proposed short-term doc patch: under "CI / reproducible installs" add a subsection "Exporting with extras" with two recommended recipes:
1) If CI uses pip and you want extras, run: `poetry export --format requirements.txt --extras "async" -o requirements.txt` and then `pip install -r requirements.txt`
2) If extras cause compatibility problems with your CI pinning policy, list explicit extras dependencies in a separate `ci-extras.txt` and `pip install -r ci-extras.txt` after base install.

yara: I can write the docs blurb. Also add a small note to CONTRIBUTING that new hires should prefer `poetry install` for local dev instead of exported requirements for quickstarts.

tom: For the repo itself, could add a tiny `scripts/export-with-extras.sh` that calls poetry export with our common extras and writes a combined `requirements-ci.txt`. That will reduce copy/paste mistakes and onboarding friction. We could also add a test in CI that runs our recommended export command and asserts `aiohttp` is present in the generated requirements file.

ci-bot: Idea: add release/packaging check that runs `poetry export --format requirements.txt --extras "async"` and verifies the resulting file contains known optional deps (e.g., `aiohttp` and `websockets` if present). Failure should block docs/CI merges.

zoe: Note for maintainers: double-check the extras key names in pyproject (`async` vs `async-client` etc.) before exporting. We've had mismatches in the past where docs used "async" but wheel metadata used "async-client". The export command uses pyproject keys.

micah: I'll open a two-part PR: 1) docs patch with the recipes and CONTRIBUTING note, 2) small scripts/export helper plus a CI test that ensures exported requirements include async extras. Will link to this thread.

docs-bot: Draft docs PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk/pull/2100 (WIP) — adds "Exporting with extras" section and troubleshooting note.

micah: Thanks. I'll add the CI test and the export script. Ping me for review. :thumbsup:
